name: Aadhar Housing Finance Ltd
title: Aadhar Housing Finance Ltd - 544176 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Aadhar's Q1 FY27 is a steady housing-finance print: AUM up 18% to ₹31,364 cr, spreads held at 5.8%, but a cheque-realisation accounting shift cut disbursement growth to about 19% on a like-for-like basis and Q1 credit cost rose seasonally.

triggers.label: Next 3 quarters disbursement >20%
triggers.quote: the next 3 quarters will be a disbursement upward of or close to about 20%.

triggers.label: Branch openings slipped to 2 in Q1
triggers.quote: we could have opened 5 to 7 branches in quarter 1. We restricted to 2.

red_flags.quote: Effective quarter 1, we have taken a step of transitioning our loan accounting to cheque clearance basis model of disbursement recognition

summary.headline: Aadhar Housing Q1 FY27 PAT rose 19% YoY to INR282 crores on AUM of INR31,364 crores (+18%), with disbursements hit by a switch to cheque-clearance recognition.
summary.overview: AUM reached INR31,364 crores, up 18% YoY, and exit spread held at 5.8% despite a 15 bps RPLR cut in February 2026. Disbursement was INR2,036 crores on the new cheque-clearance basis, against INR2,359 crores (+19% YoY) on the old cheque-handover basis, as the company moved recognition to clearance from Q1 FY27. Asset quality was stable YoY, with GNPA at 1.31% (down 3 bps) and Stage 2 at 3.3% (down 40 bps), though Q1 credit cost rose seasonally. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% AUM growth, 20% PAT growth and 17-18% disbursement growth, with the next three quarters targeted above 20%.

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: 73% of AUM; non-home loans 27%. Incremental disbursement mix currently 76:24 home vs non-home, versus a historical 70:30.

segments.name: Non-home loans
segments.commentary: Disbursement growth slowed to about 22% in the quarter by the analyst's read; management called the slowdown a deliberate choice linked to the West Asia situation and the riskier profile of these loans.

segments.name: Emerging vs urban branches
segments.commentary: About 450 of 628 branches are in emerging locations. Emerging yields are 14-14.8% versus 11.5-12% in urban; average ticket size rose only from INR10.4 lakh to INR11 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance held: 20% AUM growth, 20% PAT growth, 17-18% disbursement growth for the full year.
Disbursement growth above 20% targeted for each of the next three quarters; management expects Q2 to close the Q1 shortfall, with Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more.
July 2026 disbursement close to INR900 crores, per management.
Spread floor of 5.5% reiterated; over 2-3 years spreads expected to end near 5.5%, ROA 4.3-4.4% steady state, and ROE around 17% in a couple of years.
Cost-to-income expected to fall 30-40 bps a year; cost-to-AUM about 6-7 bps a year.
Credit cost expected to settle at 23-25 bps for the full year, with GNPA targeted at about 1.1% at year end.
Branch openings of 45-50 planned for Q3; Q1 had only 2 openings versus a 40-50 annual pace.
capex_capacity: Network at 628 branches across 22 states and 550+ districts as of June 2026.
New branches target productivity within 9-15 months; Q1 opened only 2 branches, with 5-7 planned and pushed into July.
Capital adequacy of 42.9% Tier 1 gives room for growth; the IPO's INR1,000 crores primary raise is meant to fund growth for the next 3-4 years. No plan to return capital.
Operational-risk capital set aside at about 6-7% of capital; balance-sheet risk weight about 45%.
demand_pricing: Demand described as healthy and end-user, first-time-buyer driven, particularly in emerging markets; management reports no demand-side issues in urban locations.
Spreads held at 5.8% after a 15 bps RPLR cut in February 2026; management says it protects spreads over chasing yields.
Management expects 5-7% overlap with new affordable-segment entrants; Aadhar sits one notch below in low-income housing.
Incremental yields flat QoQ; management expects no decline if the urban/emerging mix moves toward 50:50.
NRI-linked exposure described as minimal; state-level rule caps any state at 15% of AUM, incremental disbursement or distribution.
Delhi's share rose slightly, a lower-yield state, yet yields held.

financial_highlights.change: includes ~INR14 crores quarterly ESOP cost; ~33-34% excluding it

qa_highlights.question: How is the company sustaining asset yields despite the 15 bps RPLR cut and competition, and is it due to pricing, mix, or segment changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited the urban/emerging strategy (about 450 of 628 branches in emerging locations) and a ticket size that moved only from INR10.4 lakh to INR11 lakh. Delhi's share rose slightly though it is a lower-yield state, and yields still held. No major state-mix shift was reported.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to sustain 20% growth and the 5.5% spread floor amid new affordable-segment entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Book spread is about 5.8%. Management expects a 5-7% overlap with new entrants, since Aadhar sits one notch below them in low-income housing, and says the emerging tilt will keep spreads above 5.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the July disbursement number and how will the cheque-clearance change be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: July disbursement is close to INR900 crores. Management expects Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more, with Q2 substantially covering the Q1 shortfall as the carry-forward business is recognised over a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cheque-clearance change affecting interest income, and what drove the sequential employee cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest income is affected by only 2-3 days, which management called immaterial. Sequential employee cost rose on the annual increment of about 10-12%. Year-on-year, the 27% rise is mainly INR14-15 crores of quarterly ESOP cost; excluding it, employee cost growth is about 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 rise in GNPA and Stage 2 seasonal, and what is the full-year credit cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 credit cost is seasonally high at 40-45 bps for the last 2-3 years. Management expects the year to end with credit cost of 23-25 bps and GNPA near 1.1%. Q1 rose 25 bps versus a usual 30-35 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the liquidity buffer and cost-of-funds outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquidity was INR2,371 crores at quarter end, above 10% of borrowings, but management targets 7-8% intra-quarter and this rises at quarter end from drawdowns. Cost of funds moved little in Q1. Management sees no near-term impact from rate rises and says 75% of assets can be repriced.

risks_watch: Disbursement and PAT growth depend on Q2 catching up on the cheque-clearance shortfall; management targets Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more and above 20% for the next three quarters.
Non-home loan disbursement growth slowed to about 22%, and the home/non-home mix stood at 76:24 against a historical 70:30; management expects normalisation from Q3 once West Asia uncertainty eases.
Credit cost and GNPA: Q1 credit cost rose seasonally by 25 bps; the year-end GNPA target of about 1.1% and credit cost of 23-25 bps must hold.
Competitive pressure from affordable-segment entrants with a 5-7% overlap; spread floor of 5.5% and incremental yields flat QoQ.
Branch expansion slowed to 2 openings in Q1 against a 40-50 annual pace; 45-50 openings are planned for Q3 and 5-7 were pushed into July.
Cost of funds and interest-rate risk, with management expecting no imminent pass-through in the current or next quarter.
Monsoon and West Asia-related stress on rural and semi-urban cash flows, and NRI-linked exposure, which management called minimal.
key_quotes: Effective quarter 1, we have taken a step of transitioning our loan accounting to cheque clearance basis model of disbursement recognition, which is a forward -looking approach and a significant milestone in our commitment to governa nce, transparency and putting customer at the forefront.

Our approach, as always, has been to protect spreads rather than c hase yields, which we are doing by tilting the mix towards emerging branches by staying disciplined on loan against property and by continuing to drive productivity per branch and per employee, so that operating leverage does the work that pricing cannot.
And as we look at the current quarter and the upcoming quarter, which is quarter 3, we stand by our numbers of 45 to 50 branches.
So, I think Q2 itself, you will compensate the loss which we saw in Q1.
summary.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on FY27 guidance and asset quality, with management reiterating 20% AUM and PAT growth. It is more cautious on the West Asia situation, monsoon risk and non-home loan slowdown, and it defended the cheque-clearance accounting change as a governance step rather than a loss.
